# Results — Study 182 (Vortex-Indicator) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Vortex Indicator
(Botes-Siepman 2010): VI+(14)/VI−(14) crossover — enter long on VI+ crossing above VI−,
short on VI− crossing above VI+; fixed-horizon forward-return exit at 14/20 days; three
liquid ETFs (SPY, QQQ, IWM) over 10 years of daily bars (10y yfinance); compared against
a random-direction control on identical entries. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n bars | Crossovers | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| SPY | 2016-06-15 → 2026-06-15 | 2,514 | 199 | `a1f992a435bb` |
| QQQ | 2016-06-15 → 2026-06-15 | 2,514 | 201 | `dfe2803a4ed8` |
| IWM | 2016-06-15 → 2026-06-15 | 2,514 | 261 | `96907ee2e844` |

## Per-instrument breakdown (hold = 14 days, gross)

| Ticker | n crossovers | n/yr | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY** | 199 | 19.9 | 48.7% | **−10.1** | **−0.55** |
| **QQQ** | 201 | 20.1 | 53.7% | **+14.9** | **+0.57** |
| **IWM** | 261 | 26.1 | 50.2% | **+28.7** | **+1.51** |
| **Pooled** | **661** | **22.0** | **50.8%** | **+12.8** | **+1.09** |

No instrument clears |*t*| = 2 at the canonical 14-day hold. SPY is negative; QQQ and IWM
are positive but well within noise. The pooled HAC *t* of **+1.09** is
statistically indistinguishable from zero.

## The honest test — pooled crossover vs random direction (hold = 14 days, cost = 0)

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **VI crossover (with the signal)** | 661 | **50.8%** | **+12.8** | **+1.09** |
| Random direction (control) | 661 | 50.2% | −23.4 | −1.55 |

The crossover beat the random control in this sample (cross − random = **+36.2 bps/trade**),
but the cross itself does not clear the inference bar (|*t*| < 2). The coin comparison is
informative: 70% of 20 random seeds fell below the cross mean, which means the cross is
in the upper end of its distribution — but not significantly so.

## Hold-period sweep — gross, pooled (Bonferroni correction k = 5)

| Hold days | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5 | +4.2 | +0.56 |
| 10 | +8.6 | +0.91 |
| 14 | +12.8 | +1.09 |
| **20** | **+20.2** | **+1.63** |
| 30 | +10.0 | +0.76 |

The 20-day hold is the strongest (|*t*| = **1.63**). Under a Bonferroni correction for
*k* = 5 tested horizons the adjusted significance threshold is |*t*| ≈ 2.58 — the best
period **fails**. Even the unadjusted bar of 2.0 is not reached.

## Cost sweep (hold = 20 days — the best horizon)

At approximately 22 crossovers per ETF per year, costs are a modest drag but not the
primary problem — the edge is simply not statistically established:

| Round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +20.2 | +1.63 |
| 0.5 bps | +19.7 | +1.59 |
| 1.0 bps | +19.2 | +1.55 |
| 2.0 bps | +18.2 | +1.47 |
| 5.0 bps | +15.2 | +1.23 |

At 22 trades/yr, a 1 bp round-trip cost reduces the annual gross from ~4.4% to ~4.2% —
tiny. The problem is not the cost; the problem is that the gross signal does not clear the
inference bar at any cost level or any hold period.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same engine recovers
a VI crossover edge **only when bar-level momentum is planted**, and reads near zero on a
martingale — confirming the rule is a faithful momentum harvester, and that the real tape
carries at most a borderline (sub-2) signal at this horizon:

| Planted bar AR(1) momentum | cross gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0–4 (coin) | no |
| +0.15 (mild trend) | +17 | marginal |
| +0.30 (strong trend) | +35 | yes |
| −0.15 (mean-reversion) | −7 | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Best pooled gross HAC *t* = +1.63 (hold = 20d), which does not clear
  the unadjusted inference bar of 2.0, let alone the Bonferroni-corrected bar of 2.58.
  IWM alone reaches *t* = +1.51 at 14-day hold. The positive direction is consistent but
  not statistically certified on this 10-year, 3-ticker tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** At ~22 crossovers/yr, the expected annual gross
  (≈ 20 bps/trade × 22 = ~4.4%/yr) is real in sign but statistically unestablished; at
  realistic 1 bp costs the net annual return is essentially the same. A strategy built
  on a sub-2 *t* is not investable — the rule is a noise trader masquerading as a
  trend follower.
- **Beats a coin? — MIXED.** The crossover beat the random-direction control in this sample
  (70% of coin seeds fell below the cross), but the cross itself is not significant.
  A signal that does not clear 2σ cannot be certified as "better than a coin."
